alternate_mechanisms.name: naming becomes moral classification
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The surah opens by naming the one to whom praise and worship belong and closes by classifying the communities and routes that do or do not belong to divine favor.

alternate_mechanisms.name: mercy creates protected belonging
alternate_mechanisms.summary: Mercy becomes kinship-like care, lordship becomes fostered dependency, and guidance becomes refuge; the plural prayer is thus a protected mode of communal belonging rather than an isolated request.

alternate_mechanisms.name: sovereignty becomes dependable support
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The Lord and Owner is also the mainstay and source of subsistence, explaining why recognition of sovereignty turns immediately into exclusive seeking of help.

alternate_mechanisms.name: judgment as exact account settlement
alternate_mechanisms.summary: Ownership authorizes recompense, while debt, appraisal, exact measure, and legal settlement give the Day of Judgment a precise liability-and-accounting underlay.

alternate_mechanisms.name: the path as supported embodied movement
alternate_mechanisms.summary: Help enables supported walking; guidance takes a road as its object; straightness is embodied as upright progress; stoppage and exhaustion form the counter-path.

alternate_mechanisms.name: pastoral ownership beneath favor and straying
alternate_mechanisms.summary: Gathered herds and provisioned livestock materialize care and known ownership, while the stray animal materializes loss of route and detachment from that care; all animal referents remain secondary.

alternate_mechanisms.name: the worlds as an ecological provision system
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The universal created realms receive a qualified material substrate of sky, rain, plants, abundant water, reservoirs, habitat, and settlement provision under nurturing lordship.

alternate_mechanisms.name: voluntary worship contrasted with coercive control
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The sovereign's capacity to own and compel is answered by freely voiced first-person-plural worship, converting hierarchy into allegiance and covenant rather than reducing worship to forced servitude.
